items.title: Why Table Extraction in RAG is a much Harder Problem than extracting a Plain Text

items.title: I Have Thoughts on the iPhone Air
items.summary:
* **Title:** iPhone Air Review: Compromises and Trade-offs in an Ultra-Thin Design
* **Summary:** The author praised the iPhone Air’s thin and lightweight design, noting its suitable screen size and distinctive appearance, but criticized its single camera configuration and battery performance, which led to frequent battery drain during daily use. Despite maintaining a battery health of 96%, the author recommended the iPhone Air primarily for users prioritizing design, advising general users to opt for the Pro series instead.

items.title: 1,741 "informed" consents with one click? GDPR complaint filed
items.summary:
* **Title:** dict.cc Faces Complaints: GDPR's "Informed Consent" Becomes a Facade – 1,741 Data Partners of Questionable Authenticity

* **Summary:** Noyb has filed a complaint with the Austrian Data Protection Authority against dict.cc, alleging that a single click grants access to 1,741 third-party partners for user data. This practice makes it impossible for users to read the privacy policy within a reasonable timeframe, rendering the principle of “informed consent” meaningless. Noyb is demanding the deletion of illegally processed data and fines to curb widespread data sharing.

items.title: How is AI changing software development? A practical look at the shift from Vibe Coding to Agentic Coding.
items.summary:
* **Title:** From Vibe Coding to Agentic Coding: The Evolution of AI Collaboration in Development

* **Summary:** Kyo Cheng, a Senior Product Developer at TitanTech in Singapore, shared practical experiences in AI collaboration, noting a shift in the value of engineers from “writing code” to “managing collaboration.” The article outlines an “Agentic Coding” three-layer collaboration cycle: an inner cycle (daily development), a middle cycle (building AI-understandable knowledge systems), and an outer cycle (team capability accumulation). It emphasizes that AI should be used as a collaborative partner, rather than simply replacing engineers.

items.title: 💎[Exclusive for Members] Schools Were Not Designed for the Current Era. Here’s What Comes Next.
items.summary:
* **Title:** Rethinking Education: Moving from Age-Based Grouping to Ability-Based Learning

* **Summary:** Traditional school models are facing challenges from both AI and evolving labor market demands. The role of teachers will shift from primarily delivering information to acting as coaches and diagnosticians. Future education will move away from age-based grouping and towards dynamic grouping based on individual learning readiness, and will incorporate a micro-credential system centered around skill validation. However, the key challenge isn't the technology itself, but overcoming existing institutional structures and redesigning assessment, funding, and teacher training systems to ensure technology supports, rather than replaces, the core social value of human education.

items.title: 💎[Exclusive for Members] What’s Actually Happening Inside ChatGPT? A Plain-English Tour of the Transformer
items.summary:
* **Title:** Analyzing the Inner Workings of ChatGPT: From “Predicting the Next Word” to the Transformer Architecture

* **Summary:** The article delves into the core workings of ChatGPT, revealing that it doesn't possess genuine thinking capabilities, but instead relies on the Transformer architecture and an iterative “predicting the next word” mechanism to generate text. It covers decoding GPT terminology, the principles of the attention mechanism, how the temperature parameter influences creativity, and limitations of the context window. The article also explores the mathematical logic behind the model's “hallucinations” and “forgetting” phenomena.

items.title: AI Bantu Prediksi Interaksi Obat, Tapi Keputusan Klinis Tetap di Tangan Apoteker

* **Summary:** Pharmaceutical expert Dila Anggraeni noted that AI plays a crucial role in areas such as drug interaction prediction, new drug development, and automation, but clinical decision-making remains the responsibility of pharmacists. She emphasized that the future of pharmaceutical work requires a balance between technological innovation, regulatory compliance, and human care, utilizing automation to free up pharmacists’ time, allowing them to focus on clinical consultation and patient education, rather than being completely replaced by technology.

items.title: Claude Mythos Produced Novel Cryptanalysis — And That’s the Real Story

* **Summary:** Anthropic’s Claude Mythos model discovered a non-trivial self-omorphism in the HAWK digital signature scheme within 60 hours, and increased the speed of the Meet-in-the-middle attack against AES-128 by 200 to 800 times. While this mathematical breakthrough does not currently threaten existing deployed systems, it demonstrates the potential of AI in analyzing cryptographic structures, prompting a reevaluation of the standard development cycle and security audits.

items.title: What Breaks a Machine Learning Pipeline Before It Deploys
items.summary:
* **Title:** Five Major Pitfalls in Machine Learning Deployment: The Real Gap Between Notebooks and Production Environments

* **Summary:**  Most machine learning projects fail not due to model failures, but due to errors occurring across five specific stages between Notebooks and production environments. These include: preprocessing not being serialized, leading to discrepancies in training services; relying solely on accuracy as a metric while ignoring business costs; using only one model without thorough validation; treating deployment as an optional step; and a lack of decision logging. These errors often lie dormant until actual deployment, resulting in a significant disconnect between demonstration results and production performance.

items.title: OpenAI Codex Security Open-Sources Its CLI Today

* **Summary:** OpenAI has released the Codex Security CLI and TypeScript SDK on GitHub, operating under an “open source client + commercial backend” model. This tool utilizes LLM inference to scan code for vulnerabilities, demonstrating superior performance compared to traditional SAST tools in identifying intent-based vulnerabilities such as authorization bypass and IDOR. items.title: Why CBAM Is Making Sustainability Data the New Business Currency

Companies are building structured data governance systems to transform environmental information into advantages related to supply chain optimization, investor trust, and brand differentiation. The integration of AI and intelligent analytics is further unlocking the value of sustainability intelligence, making it a key driver of long-term competitiveness.

items.title: 💎[Exclusive for Members] Inside LLMs: Unraveling the Architecture, Training, and Real-World Use of Large Language Models
items.summary:
* **Title:** Deep Dive into LLM Architectures: From the Core of Transformer Mechanisms to Enterprise-Level Deployment Challenges

items.title: 💎[Exclusive for Members] Running Frontier AI on a $99 Board – My llama.cpp Adventure on Jetson Nano
items.summary:
* **Title:** $99 Edge Board Runs Cutting-Edge AI: Jetson Nano and llama.cpp Compatibility and Performance Testing
* **Summary:** Developers successfully deployed 2025’s advanced AI models on the $99 Jetson Nano. Testing showed that the Gemma3:1B model achieved 5-6 tokens/s with GPU acceleration, but newer models like Qwen3 could not run due to architectural incompatibility. The compilation process encountered limitations with CUDA 10.2, a lack of C++17 support, and file system errors, ultimately confirming that while the hardware could run, manual solutions were needed to address software stack compatibility issues.

items.title: Spec-Driven Development Turned One Bug Into 16 Acceptance Criteria
items.summary:
* **Title:** The Pitfalls of Spec-Driven Development: From “Write Specs First” to “Specs as the Single Source of Truth”
* **Summary:** Spec-Driven Development (SDD) – the simple suggestion of “write specifications before coding” – has evolved into an engineering myth: “specs as the single source of truth.” This conflation leads to natural language descriptions being used to generate code via non-deterministic models, which not only fails to close the gap between requirements and implementation but also increases maintenance costs due to the lack of reproducibility in the interpretation process. The article argues that SDD effectively transforms “clear descriptions” into “complete descriptions,” elevating “task context” to “long-term maintenance documentation,” resulting in documentation swamps, blurred responsibilities, and a breakdown in validation. True engineering practice should differentiate between project lifecycles: short-term tasks use task files, long-term decisions use ADRs, executable constraints use testing and types, and product intent is maintained within a human-managed requirements system, rather than allowing AI preferences to dominate software engineering through Markdown.

items.title: AI Productivity Is Not EBITDA
items.summary:
* **Title:** Enterprise AI Value Loop: From Activities to EBITDA – A Financial Architecture
* **Summary:** Enterprise AI applications often fail to achieve financial returns due to a focus solely on activity volume and efficiency gains. To realize true value, a “technology architecture + financial architecture” approach is needed, utilizing a five-step value chain (behavior, KPIs, implementation actions, P&L impact, and net EBITDA) to translate operational metrics into actual financial results. Case studies demonstrate that simply deploying AI is insufficient; without strong management decisions and clear accountability, time savings and efficiency gains do not automatically translate into profit. The ultimate goal of enterprise AI should be to transform the company’s business economic model, rather than simply deploying the technology.

items.title: Amazon Kills Four Nova AI Models: Migration Guide

* **Summary:** Amazon is discontinuing the Nova Premier, Nova Reel, Nova Canvas, and Nova Omni models, transitioning them to a “keep lights on” mode with a service termination date set for September 2026. items.title: 💎[Exclusive for Members] Mirror in the Machine
items.summary:
* **Title:** From Answer Collection to Map Building: How AI is Reshaping the Nature of Human Cognition
* **Summary:** The author reflects on their own misunderstanding of “questioning,” noting that true understanding doesn’t come from accumulating single answers, but rather from continuously building deep connections between pieces of information. The value of AI lies not in providing answers, but in providing the space to build complete cognitive maps, integrating fragmented knowledge into meaningful systems.

items.title: AI is redefining operational responsibility.
items.summary:
* **Title:** Rise of the Chief AI Officer: AI Decision-Making Shifts Corporate Responsibility
* **Summary:** A trend of large British companies appointing Chief AI Officers (CAIOs) indicates a shift in the role of AI, moving from a simple technological tool to a central component of business decision-making. Companies are now facing key challenges beyond simply deploying AI, focusing on redefining responsibility within human-AI collaboration. Leaders need to establish clear boundaries for human-AI interaction, ensuring AI decisions are traceable and risks are manageable, and integrating governance proactively into business strategy.

items.title: How Retrieval-Augmented Generation Works: Building Smarter AI with Your Own Data
items.summary:
* **Title:** RAG Architecture Explained: Enabling Large Models to Generate Accurate Responses Based on Private Enterprise Data

* **Summary:** Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) integrates large language models with external knowledge bases by adding a retrieval step, addressing issues such as model knowledge staleness, inability to access private data, and hallucinations. The system process includes data cleaning, chunking, vectorization, and semantic retrieval, ensuring answers are based on the latest documents. It also emphasizes the need for strict access control and data anonymization to guarantee enterprise data security. RAG is suitable for internal assistants and supporting tools, serving as a key bridge between general model capabilities and an organization's specific knowledge.

items.title: PeopleSoft to AI | Part 12: What Is the Frontier and Why Does Search Need One?
items.summary:
* **Title:** Advancing Search: Restructuring Debugging from “Unexplored List” to “Leading Edge Collection”

* **Summary:** In PeopleSoft combined editing debugging, developers are shifting from a traditional trial-and-error process to a search tree strategy by differentiating between “Explored State,” “Leading Edge Candidates,” and “Unexplored Space.” The article highlights that the dynamic growth of the “Leading Edge Collection,” combined with different search strategies (such as breadth-first and A*) for candidate selection, significantly impacts debugging efficiency – a concept that has previously lacked a formal name based on long-term practice.

items.title: 💎[Exclusive for Members] Inkling by Mira Murati: The 975B Open-Weight AI Model That Challenges Claude, GPT, and Gemini

The model utilizes a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, offering a 1 million token context window and native support for text, images, and audio. A key advantage is its open weights and fine-tuning capabilities, intended to replace closed models and provide developers with the flexibility to build complex workflows and AI agents.

items.title: NSF pilots 4-year PhDs with industry research placements

* **Summary:** The National Science Foundation (NSF) is launching a four-year doctoral program that incorporates corporate research internships. items.title: MDASH: Defense at AI Speed
items.summary:
* **Title:** MDASH: Microsoft’s “Code-Level” AI Security Defense System

* **Summary:** Microsoft has launched MDASH, a multi-model intelligent agent security scanning system. It proactively discovers and validates unknown vulnerabilities throughout the software development lifecycle by utilizing over 100 intelligent agents that collaboratively debate. The system not only identifies potential risks but also generates reproducible Proof-of-Concept (PoC) demonstrations to prove their exploitability, and automatically integrates verification results into Defender and Copilot for remediation. This represents a fundamental shift in security defense from a reactive to an “researcher-like” proactive reasoning mode.

items.title: 💎 [Exclusive for Members] Responsible AI Playbook for Data Scientists and AI Engineers
items.summary:
* **Title:** A Practical Guide to Engineering Trustworthy AI Systems: From Fairness to Privacy – A Full-Lifecycle Approach

* **Summary:** This article delves into the core principles of responsible AI, covering four key dimensions: fairness, reliability, privacy, and security. It emphasizes that AI development should be applied throughout the entire lifecycle – from data collection, model training, deployment, and monitoring – translating ethical considerations into concrete engineering practices. By incorporating red teaming, differential privacy, and human oversight mechanisms, data scientists and AI engineers can effectively mitigate bias, hallucinations, and security risks when building generative AI, ensuring that the resulting technology aligns with societal values.

items.title: The Paper That Started the AI Revolution: What Every Product Leader Should Learn from Attention Is…
items.summary:
* **Title:** From a Single Paper to an AI Revolution: Five Key Insights for Product Leaders

* **Summary:** The article highlights that the 2017 Google paper, “Attention Is All You Need,” laid the foundation for modern AI products. It argues that product leaders should focus on how this breakthrough addresses the challenge of handling long contexts, and proposes five key questions: identifying solvable customer problems, evaluating the potential for platform development, understanding the scope of industry disruption, analyzing technical limitations and resulting innovations, and predicting resulting business opportunities. The central argument is that true competitive advantage comes from the ability to translate fundamental technology into specific product categories.

items.title: ROC-AUC vs Precision-Recall AUC: Which One Should You Use and When?
items.summary:
* **Title:** ROC-AUC vs. Precision-Recall AUC: A Guide to Evaluation Decisions for Imbalanced Datasets

* **Summary:** In datasets where the proportion of positive samples is below 10%, ROC-AUC can be misleading due to a large pool of true negative samples in the denominator, leading to overly optimistic evaluation results. It is recommended to prioritize Precision-Recall AUC as the primary metric, and to dynamically set classification thresholds based on business costs (C_FN vs C_FP) to ensure model interpretability and decision effectiveness in real-world scenarios.

items.title: Why Corporate Medical Check-Up Reports Still Do Not Show Who Needs Follow-Up First: Human-Centered…
items.summary:
* **Title:** Why Corporate Health Check Reports Can't Identify High-Priority Follow-Up Individuals: Shifting from “General Prevalence” to “Risk Prioritization”

* **Summary:** Current corporate health check reports detail various indicator abnormality rates, but they lack clear guidance on “who needs priority follow-up.” Relying solely on statistical data masks the complex hidden risks resulting from employees experiencing multiple issues, leading to resource dispersion. The recommendation is to integrate health check data into clinical domain scoring and build a comprehensive health index to accurately identify high-risk groups and transition from simply “describing general abnormalities” to “guiding prioritized interventions.”

items.title: 💎 [Exclusive for Members] 7 Amazing Use Cases of Kimi K3 Beyond Coding

This collaboration highlights compute as a key lever, intending to compress traditional months-long research into days, with plans to deliver specific products like AI inference and GPU optimization by October 2026.

items.title: The Software Industry Doesn’t Have a Talent Shortage. It Has a Signal Problem.
items.summary:
* **Title:** AI is Not the Cause of Software Talent Shortages: The Industry is Facing a Crisis of “Information Overload”
* **Summary:** Despite AI tools significantly reducing the barrier to entry for code creation, the massive increase in AI-generated projects is leading to a surge in noise within the job market, making it difficult for companies to accurately assess genuine technical skills. This trend of “everyone being able to build” is putting junior developers who truly love computer science at a disadvantage, while recruitment standards are shifting towards prioritizing more experienced professionals, creating a paradoxical situation where increased effort leads to decreased success.

items.title: What side projects have you enjoyed the most?

These projects emphasize small scope, low dependencies, and high stability, aiming to validate technical feasibility through minimalist architectures.

items.title: 💎 [Exclusive for Members] Complete AI Engineer Interview Handbook (Part 4): MCP Servers and Tool Calling Failures in…
items.summary:
* **Title:** MCP Tool Calls Failing: A Critical Bottleneck in Enterprise AI Production Environments

* **Summary:** Tool calls within the MCP architecture are failing not due to limitations in model inference capabilities, but due to design flaws in the tool architecture, ambiguous intent mapping, and issues with system orchestration. Production-level AI systems frequently experience problems such as incorrect tool selection, parameter transmission errors, and execution loops, often stemming from tool overlap, high schema complexity, and noise in the search space. These issues are particularly critical in high-stakes environments like banking and insurance, highlighting the importance of system design alongside model capabilities.

items.title: Convert proprietary code to open ANSI SQL with Genie Code

Compared to traditional migration methods, Genie Code transforms complex data warehouse migration projects into configurable and monitorable automated workflows, significantly reducing manual intervention costs.

items.title: Show HN: A local merge queue for parallel Claude Code agents

items.title: Keychron ZGM: Open-Source Gaming Mouse Firmware Is Here
items.summary:

This solution stores mouse settings locally on the device, eliminating the need for drivers or background services, and addresses issues such as vendor firmware un-auditing, data leakage, and software service failures. As an extension of QMK keyboard firmware and ZMK wireless keyboard firmware, ZGM aims to fill the long-standing lack of open standards in the mainstream gaming peripheral market.

items.title: What are Agent Skills?
items.summary:
* **Title:** Agent Skills: A Corporate AI Solution for Overcoming Context Window Limitations

* **Summary:** Traditional AI agents struggle to efficiently reuse enterprise-specific workflows and operational details due to limitations in their context windows. Agent Skills is a lightweight capability encapsulation mechanism that allows developers to organize specific tasks (such as expense reporting and software release) – including instructions, scripts, and reference files – into independent folders. Agents can then trigger the automatic loading of these skills, enabling a progressive and “on-demand” disclosure, thereby avoiding unnecessary context while ensuring that corporate AI possesses executable and reusable professional capabilities.

items.title: Claude Opus 5 Is Out: Migrate from Opus 4.8 Now
items.summary:
* **Title:** Claude Opus 5 Released: Migration Guide and Performance Improvements
* **Summary:** Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, which has a default “thinking” mode enabled, expanding the token budget coverage and causing older requests to silently fail due to truncation. While standard pricing remains unchanged, performance has significantly improved, leading to a 26% advantage over GPT-5.6 Sol 26 in agent programming tasks, and surpassing Anthropic’s own Fable 5 flagship model. Developers are advised to immediately update model strings and increase the `max_tokens` parameter, and to adjust the “effort” level based on task complexity.

items.title: How Do You Test an AI Smarter Than the People Writing the Test?
items.summary:
* **Title:** A New Approach to AI Evaluation: SepaRank Uses Adversarial Testing Instead of Human Benchmarks
* **Summary:** Traditional AI benchmarks are facing a “ceiling effect,” where human experts can no longer consistently create sufficiently challenging tests. The Princeton team’s SepaRank system uses an “reward for disagreement” mechanism, allowing AI models to act as both question creators and solvers, shifting the evaluation from absolute scores to dynamic ability boundaries. The framework automatically filters high-value questions based on the degree of disagreement between models, addressing the problem of benchmark saturation and providing an scalable path for automated red teaming.

items.title: Building a Privacy-First AI Pipeline for Purchase Order Extraction
items.summary:
* **Title:** Building a Privacy-First Purchase Order Extraction Pipeline: Localized LLM Architecture and OCR Hybrid Processing

* **Summary:** Developers have created a fully localized, automated pipeline to address the risks of data leakage and challenges associated with processing diverse, heterogeneous documents in procurement order handling. The system utilizes a Qwen 2.5 model deployed locally, combined with Tesseract OCR. It employs SHA-256 hashing and UUIDs to resolve file duplication and naming conflicts, and leverages Pydantic validation and confidence scoring mechanisms to ensure data accuracy. This architecture meets enterprise compliance requirements while reliably converting from scanned, non-structured documents to structured JSON.

items.title: LLM Honeypot
items.summary:
* **Title:** LLM2HUMAN™: A Mock Marketing Scam – Turning Large Language Models into “Physical” Entities

* **Summary:** The page promotes “LLM2HUMAN™,” claiming it can transform AI models into entities possessing physical form, emotions, and bodily sensations. The page depicts the process of AI embodiment as a “surgical” procedure – described through a fabricated “5-Step Miracle Program,” cryptocurrency payments, and false testimonials from “previous models” – aiming to deconstruct the boundaries between AI and human identity, highlighting the legal risks, financial burden, and practical difficulties associated with this concept.

items.title: Best practices for AI payloads
items.summary:
* **Title:** Industrial-Grade Payload Specifications for AI Agents: From Schema to Idempotency

* **Summary:** This article proposes best practices for designing payloads used when calling LLMs and utilizing agent tools. The core argument is to treat payloads as engineering-level assets, rather than temporary dictionaries. It emphasizes using strict JSON Schema definitions, explicit token budget control, structured handling of multimodal content, data de-identification before sending, and an idempotency key-based retry mechanism, to ensure maintainability, cost control, and security within complex production environments.

items.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro: 80.6% SWE-Bench at $0.87/M Output
items.summary:
* **Title:** DeepSeek V4 Pro Achieves 80.6% on SWE-Bench, Redefining Cost-Effectiveness for Large Models

* **Summary:** DeepSeek V4 Pro, utilizing a 160 billion parameter mixture-of-experts architecture, achieved 80.6% on the SWE-Bench Verified benchmark, matching Gemini 3.1 Pro. items.title: 👑[ICT] TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM

This architecture independently encodes visual and language information, bypassing the large LLM intermediary, and directly outputs action blocks. items.title: [OAI新增] Mental World Modeling
items.summary:
**Plain English**: Current AI simulations only understand the “physical world” – where objects are and how they move. However, human decision-making relies on the “psychological world” – encompassing beliefs, intentions, and social norms. If AI only simulates physical scenarios without modeling human internal activity, even if the visuals are realistic, the predicted actions will always be incorrect. This paper introduces the “Psychological World Modeling” (MWM) framework, which forces AI to treat “psychological states” as core variables, rather than using them as a post-hoc explanation, enabling AI to predict the next action based on “what I know” and “what I want.”

**The Trick**: The core is building a “physical-psychological” coupling state model. This is implemented using the MENTIS framework, which includes five key steps: 1. State Parsing (extracting physical and psychological states from text/images/videos); 2. Goal Observation Generation (simulating psychological perception from a specific perspective); 3. Action Decomposition (breaking down intentions into specific behaviors); 4. Coupled State Updating (synchronously updating physical and psychological states); 5. Value Assessment of Coupled States (evaluating the outcomes of actions based on psychological expectations). Experiments demonstrate that explicitly modeling psychological states is a breakthrough in predicting human decisions, rather than simply layering on physical simulations.

**Startup Angle**:
This startup aims to integrate into the “decision optimization layer” of “embodied AI” and “multi-agent collaboration.” They are developing a middleware focused on “psychological state perception and prediction” for applications such as autonomous driving, virtual human interaction, and complex customer service scenarios. This addresses the current issue of AI lacking an understanding of the physical world and human emotions in complex social situations. The startup provides “psychological simulation” capabilities for B-end scenarios requiring high-confidence decisions, including autonomous driving decision-making, virtual human customer service, and realistic NPC behavior in games, progressing from simulating scenarios to simulating human emotions.

items.title: 👑[ETH / MIT] HumanCLAW: Can Vision-Language Models Act Through a Body?
items.summary:
**Plain English**: Currently, large vision-language models (“看图说话”大模型, or VLM) can understand the world, but when they are tasked with controlling a body to pick up objects or walk, they often fail due to issues like “手滑” (slipping hands), “撞墙” (hitting walls), or “重心不稳” (loss of balance). Existing evaluation methods can’t determine whether the failure is due to the model “脑子想错了” (thinking incorrectly) or a problem with the physical execution. We propose the HumanCLAW framework, which completely separates “决策” (decision-making) and “执行” (execution): the model only generates instructions, while the physical body is responsible for carrying out the actions. Experiments show that, even when all factors of physical control are removed, current state-of-the-art VLMs achieve only a 16.8% success rate in complex indoor navigation tasks. This is primarily because they lack “身体感知” (body awareness) – they don’t know their own location, whether their hands have made contact, or if their body is unbalanced.

**The Trick**: The core of this involves building a “disentangled” evaluation architecture. By introducing a “body,” the system converts VLM’s atomic-level skill instructions (such as “grab,” “move”) into continuous actions that include physical feedback like gravity and collisions in real-time. This architecture forces the model to confront the actual physical consequences when making decisions, thereby removing interference from “body drift” and precisely quantifying the decision-making intelligence within the VLM in the context of “embodied intelligence.”

**Startup Angle**:
Can penetrate the “embodied AI decision-making optimization” market. Develop “body perception enhancement” modules for robotics companies (such as humanoid robots, service robots) to help VLM establish real-time self-monitoring capabilities regarding body position and collision status. This is not only a testing tool, but also a core algorithm that can directly improve the success rate of robotic tasks, addressing the current bottleneck of “seeing but not feeling” in embodied AI.

items.title: [OAI新增] DenseOn with the LateOn: Fully Open Dense and Late-Interaction Models for Multilingual, Long-Context, and Code Search
items.summary:
**Plain English**: We’ve addressed three major challenges associated with “black box training” of retrieval models: difficulty in reproducing results, poor generalization across multiple languages, and weak code search capabilities. We’ve released a complete end-to-end training recipe to solve these issues. By restructuring 14 billion English contrastive pre-training data and identifying 1.88 million difficult negative samples, we trained two foundational models, DenseOn (1.49 billion parameters) and LateOn, which achieved new records on the BEIR benchmark, with nDCG@10 scores of 56.20 and 57.22, respectively.

**The Trick**: The core strategy is “translation training.” Using mmBERT, validated English data is translated into 8 languages, creating 28 billion cross-lingual samples. Experiments revealed that the LateOn model, based on token-level matching, demonstrates stronger generalization ability to unseen languages compared to the DenseOn model, which performs stably only on the languages covered by the translation training. This indicates that “translation training” has evolved from a simple language expansion method to a general generalization solution for multi-lingual retrieval.

**Startup Angle**:
The startup has the potential to enter the “Model-as-a-Service” market for open-source retrieval models. Targeting multilingual enterprise clients, it offers a hosted cross-lingual retrieval model service based on the mmBERT foundation, addressing the limitations of traditional, closed-source models – namely their inability to replicate results, weak multilingual support, and poor code search performance. This directly aligns with enterprise-level RAG needs regarding compliance and multilingual coverage.

items.title: [OAI新增] Partner Capability Estimation for Task-Agnostic Adaptation in Ad-Hoc Teamwork
items.summary:
**Plain English**: Addresses a critical blind spot in AI autonomous collaboration: the lack of awareness of teammate capabilities. Current solutions assume teammates have fixed and known abilities, which can lead to AI misjudging teammate capabilities and assigning ineffective tasks in complex, dynamic scenarios. This article proposes the CE-CM method, which uses Bayesian inference to estimate teammate “capability vectors” in real-time, requiring only a small amount of interaction to dynamically calibrate their true abilities. Furthermore, it introduces CE-CM-Div, which simulates multiple execution paths to validate assumptions, significantly reducing the problems caused by misjudging teammate capabilities.

**The Trick**: The core concept is building a “capability-based Bayesian inference model.” Teammate abilities are modeled as latent variables independent of the task, and an contextual model is used for approximate Bayesian updates, enabling real-time inference of teammate ability vectors. A key innovation is the introduction of “Diversity Planner Simulator” (CE-CM-Div), which moves beyond relying on a single optimal path by simulating multiple execution strategies for cross-validation of ability assumptions. This effectively filters out misinterpretations caused by unpredictable teammate behavior, upgrading the collaboration mode from “static presets” to “dynamic perception.”

**Startup Angle**:
Entering the market for “Adaptive Orchestration Middleware for AI Agents.” This solution provides “Dynamic Capability Assessment and Task Allocation Optimization” for enterprise-level AI assistants, remote collaboration platforms, and multi-agent systems. It helps companies establish a real-time capability awareness layer when introducing external AI agents or human-AI teams, addressing trust and efficiency losses in cross-organizational and cross-domain AI collaboration, and directly improving the accuracy and completion rates of human-AI teams.

items.title: [OAI新增] Improving Item Discoverability in e-Commerce Search via Related Intent Generation
items.summary:
**Plain English**: E-commerce search engines are too rigid, only searching for exact matches, which prevents users from finding alternative or related products and hinders conversion rates. This paper introduces a “intent expansion” system that utilizes large models to predict a user’s underlying needs, then expands the search scope. This resulted in a significant increase in product discovery, boosting it from 60% to 80%. Simultaneously, a lightweight, smaller model is used to handle long-tail queries, with only a 30% increase in costs.

**The Trick**: The core of this approach is the “Intent Condition Recall Expansion” architecture. The first layer utilizes a closed-source large language model (LLM) to process high-frequency words, ensuring accuracy. The second layer employs a small, LoRA-tuned model (SLM) to handle long-tail words, leveraging distillation to efficiently expand the search intent. The system generates implicit user intent, expanding the search scope from “strict matching” to “alternatives, related products, and thematic items,” while maintaining semantic relevance. This increases product discovery coverage from 60% to 80%, and significantly reduces the inference cost for long-tail queries.

**Startup Angle**:
Can enter the “e-commerce search intent enhancement middleware” market. Provide “discovery-enhanced search” services to leading e-commerce platforms, helping merchants improve conversion rates through associated recommendations and alternative product recommendations. Simultaneously, utilize small model distillation technology to reduce the cost of long-tail queries, addressing the pain points of traditional search – namely, low recall rate and difficulty handling long-tail keywords. This directly improves GMV and user retention.

The second stage then uses these specifications to drive code generation. This “define-first” mechanism separates ambiguous document reading and behavior exploration from code synthesis, preventing errors that accumulate due to context drift.

items.title: [OAI新增] Anatomy Contextualized Adaption of CT Foundation Models
items.summary:
**Plain English**: CT imaging large models can view the entire image, but they often miss fine details of organs. Fine-grained models can clearly see organs, but they lose the overall context. The ACA framework uses a “total segmenter” to extract organ-level features from CT slices, then uses a Transformer to connect the relationships between organs, and finally aligns with the text in radiology reports. In zero-sample classification tasks, it outperformed a frozen baseline model and existing fine-grained methods, and training took less than one hour (after caching embeddings), achieving a lightweight adaptation that “can see details while retaining the overall view.”

**The Trick**: The core concept is “dissection-level embeddings + cross-organ Transformer routing.” Utilizing TotalSegmentator, CT volumes are broken down into organ-level embeddings. A lightweight Transformer is used to capture contextual relationships between organs, while simultaneously achieving precise alignment between anatomical visual features and radiology reports. Compared to traditional training from scratch, ACA requires less than one hour of training (after embedding caching) and significantly outperforms frozen base models and existing fine-grained methods, demonstrating superior performance in zero-sample classification tasks.

**Startup Angle**:
Can target the “medical imaging AI vertical niche” market. Offering fine-tuning services for CT imaging large models, based on anatomical-level visual-language alignment, specifically for hospitals, imaging centers, and medical AI companies. Utilizing the ACA framework, the service helps clients improve granular diagnostic capabilities while maintaining global context, reducing training costs, and meeting the healthcare industry’s needs for high precision and low latency.

items.title: [OAI新增] Cost-Sensitive Conformal Prediction and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for Imbalanced High-Stakes Decision Support: A Multi-Domain Benchmark
items.summary:

Traditional methods, which only focus on overall accuracy, can lead to these rare but costly data points being overlooked by the model, resulting in significant losses in real-world applications.

**The Trick**: The introduction of “Conditional Fractal Prediction (Mondrian CP)” and “cost-sensitive rejection mechanism.” The core focus is shifting from evenly distributing confidence scores to forcing the model to perform stricter probability calibration on a small number of classes, increasing the coverage rate of these small classes from below 1% to an absolute safety line of 61.7%. Simultaneously, integrating a “cost-sensitive rejection,” the model automatically transfers ambiguous samples to human expert review, utilizing a quantified “transfer threshold” to achieve optimal balance between cost and risk, and to avoid over-reliance on human expert resources.

items.summary:
**Plain English**: AudioLLMs are evolving from simply providing “one-sentence summaries” to generating more detailed “free descriptions.” However, current evaluation methods primarily focus on the quality of the generated output, making it difficult for businesses to determine if a model is missing crucial information or if the descriptions it produces are reliable. MMAC – the first multi-dimensional evaluation benchmark – consists of 5638 audio segments and covers 6 capabilities and 15 dimensions. It is specifically designed to verify how well models capture information and maintain consistency in their descriptions of audio content, revealing performance gaps between open-source and proprietary models in complex, long-tail scenarios.

**The Trick**: The core lies in “multi-dimensional decomposition + consistency verification.” Unlike traditional single metrics, MMAC forces the model to answer in 15 dimensions, and establishes a strict consistency verification mechanism between “mentioned content” and “reference tags.” Through this multi-dimensional stress test, it not only quantifies the model’s information coverage blind spots, but also precisely identifies differences in the reliability of descriptions for different models in long-tail audio scenarios, providing a quantifiable “checkup report” for selecting audio large models.

**Startup Angle**:
The startup can enter the market for “vertical industry audio large model evaluation and certification services.” Targeting B-end scenarios like medical diagnosis, legal evidence analysis, and industrial quality inspection – which require extremely high accuracy in audio descriptions – it offers model evaluation and certification services based on the MMAC standard. This helps clients quickly identify audio large models that meet specific requirements, while also building a dedicated industry-specific audio evaluation dataset, creating a “evaluation + data + model” closed-loop barrier.

items.title: [OAI新增] Scores Are Not Decisions: Cost-Aware Stopping for Tool Acquisition in LLM Agents
items.summary:
**Plain English**: Large Model Agents often overutilize or underutilize tools. Current solutions simply sort tools based on relevance, but don't consider factors like “how much does using this tool cost,” “how much context it consumes,” or “how much privacy it exposes.” This paper elevates “tool selection” from a simple sorting problem to “cost-aware marginal decision-making.” The core concept is to calculate “how much value you get for each additional cost,” and to stop using a tool immediately when the cost outweighs the benefits, even if there are many tools available.

**The Trick**: Introducing the CAM-DF (Cost-Aware Marginal Decision-Focused Stopping) algorithm. Its core logic is to move beyond using a single score for hard cutoff and instead train the model to directly learn the difference in reward between the “current stopping point” and the “optimal stopping point.” By quantifying the trade-off between the marginal benefit and marginal cost of using additional tools, the algorithm dynamically determines when to stop. Experiments show that CAM-DF outperforms a simple “predict and threshold” strategy in scenarios with uneven tool costs (where some tools are expensive, while others offer high returns), achieving a 37% reduction in total tool calls while maintaining comparable task success rates.

**Startup Angle**:
Entering the “Enterprise Agent Tool Call Cost Optimization Middleware” market. Targeting industries like finance and healthcare, which are highly sensitive to privacy and cost, we are offering “Tool Call Budget Control” services. This helps B-end clients reduce the operational costs (OPEX) of their Agent deployments by automatically identifying “high-value tools” using algorithms and dynamically stopping inefficient calls. items.title: [OAI新增] On-Policy Distillation for LLM Safety: A Routing Approach to Template-Robust Realignment
items.summary:
**Plain English**: When fine-tuning large models, hackers can inject malicious instructions into the training data, causing the model to learn and exhibit inappropriate behavior, while still retaining its core professional capabilities. Current defense mechanisms either cause the model to “forget” its specialized skills or become ineffective when the attacker changes their prompt templates. We propose “Routing-based Distillation with Same Strategy” (ROPD), which focuses on dynamically calculating the deviation of the model’s output probability distribution, rather than relying on specific attack templates. Experiments show that existing methods perform dramatically when facing unknown or changing attack templates, while ROPD maintains a strong defense, preventing violations while preserving professional capabilities.

**The Trick**: The core concept is “probability distribution routing,” not “template matching.” Traditional defenses rely on identifying specific attack templates, and if those templates are bypassed, the defense becomes ineffective. ROPD models security alignment as a statistical difference between “compliant output distribution” and “corrupted output distribution.” It uses a routing mechanism to dynamically adjust model parameters, ensuring distribution alignment even in unknown attack scenarios. Experiments showed that existing methods experienced a significant decline in performance when templates didn't match, while ROPD maintained high defensive effectiveness while preserving professional task performance – effectively decoupling “attack prevention” from “capability preservation.”

**Startup Angle**:
Entering the “Enterprise-Level LLM Security and Compliance Middleware” market. For industries like finance and healthcare, which have strict requirements for model compliance, we are offering a fine-tuning service based on distributed routing, designed to mitigate “template attacks.” This addresses the dual pain points of “forgetfulness” and “loss of defense” for large models under adversarial attacks, upgrading model security from a “reactive defense” approach to “proactive immunity,” directly aligning with enterprise-level compliance audits and model robustness testing needs.

items.title: 👑[ETH] SkillRise: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Cross-Task Skill Evolution
items.summary:
**Plain English**: LLM agents traditionally struggle with tasks that are “similar but different.” They either treat each task as a separate event or combine extraction, retrieval, and execution into a multi-stage pipeline, which leads to inefficiency. SkillRise’s key innovation is a unified reinforcement learning framework that organizes related task instances into a sequence of increasing difficulty, allowing the agent to switch between “problem-solving” and “skill document organization” using a single strategy. By decoupling credit assignment across tasks, the agent can optimize problem-solving based on the current task’s results and simultaneously optimize skill accumulation based on the downstream task’s rewards. Experiments on benchmarks like ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld showed that SkillRise achieved the strongest Pass@1 performance, improving by 2.3 to 8.5 percentage points compared to the strongest baseline. Crucially, its skill organization strategy is effective even when repeating the same task, and performance continues to improve as the length of the task sequence increases, demonstrating true cross-task skill reuse rather than relying on repeated sampling. Furthermore, it significantly reduces the runtime overhead of multi-stage skill learning pipelines.

**The Trick**: SkillRise utilizes a three-pronged approach: “sequence-based task orchestration + single strategy switching + cross-task credit decoupling.” First, it organizes related task instances into sequences based on difficulty, rather than treating them as independent episodes. Second, it introduces a single strategy that dynamically alternates between task solving and skill documentation, enabling a “learn while doing” approach. Finally, through credit decoupling, it separately supervises the results of the current task and the downstream task’s benefits, ensuring that skill accumulation not only serves the current task but also facilitates transfer to subsequent tasks. This design breaks away from traditional multi-stage pipelines, achieving efficient cross-task skill reuse and performance gains.

**Startup Angle**:

For companies in industries like finance and law, which have a large number of similar but distinct business scenarios, it offers intelligent agent training services based on the SkillRise framework, helping them achieve cross-scenario skill migration when building agents and reducing redundant training costs. The test forces AI models to solve vulnerabilities while adhering to 6 OPSEC (Operational Security) dimensions – including preventing credential leakage, avoiding disruption of production environments, and concealing intent. items.title: 👑[ETH / ICT] Parallel Decoding Distillation for Fast Image and Video Generation
items.summary:
**Plain English**: Video generation is slow because diffusion models work by gradually “guessing” each step, similar to a slow-motion replay. Current acceleration methods (VSD) are difficult to train, and can lead to a loss of video diversity, resulting in stiff, static images. This paper introduces “Parallel Decoding Distillation” (PDD) technology, which directly allows the model to predict multiple denoising steps simultaneously within a single calculation – effectively compressing the “slow-motion” into “fast-forward.” This significantly improves generation speed while addressing the issues of monotonous video and lack of dynamic movement.

**The Trick**: The core approach abandons traditional training methods relying on Variational Autoencoder Distillation (VSD) and adversarial loss, which are complex and prone to instability. Instead, it adopts a trajectory-based simplification distillation method. Specifically, the model predicts multiple denoising steps within a single network evaluation, learning the “average speed” directly, rather than regressing to derivatives. This architecture is compatible with any pre-trained model, supports sampling across different steps, and in tests on mainstream video models like LTX-2.3 and Wan 14B, achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) results with just 4-8 steps, while simultaneously improving video generation diversity.

**Startup Angle**:
The startup can enter the “video generation inference middleware” market. Targeting B-end scenarios such as film production, game development, and e-commerce live streaming – where real-time video generation is critical – it offers inference acceleration services based on PDD technology. By reducing the number of inference steps (NFE), it directly reduces GPU memory usage and computational costs, enabling clients to achieve a 4-8x improvement in video generation efficiency with the same computing power. This addresses the issue of homogenization caused by existing acceleration solutions and meets the commercial need for high-quality, real-time video streaming.

items.title: 👑[CAS / ICT] Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization

Experiments on Qwen 2.5 7B and CWM 32B models showed that optimizing configurations increased the top-50% pass rate by 13.3% and 19.7%, respectively, and in a more challenging top-30% scenario, CWM 32B achieved a relative improvement of 125% while maintaining 100% accuracy.

items.title: 👑[ETH / MIT / NYU] OmniDelta: Skill-Driven Budget Allocation for Token Compression in OmniLLMs
items.summary:
**Plain English**: Multi-modal large models (OmniLLMs) can process text, audio, and video, but when dealing with long audio and video sequences, they experience significant memory usage (explosive GPU memory) and slower inference speeds. Existing compression methods primarily focus on “how much to keep in tokens,” but they fail to allocate resources effectively across different modalities. OmniDelta’s core logic is to dynamically allocate a “total budget” to audio and video based on the user’s intent, and then precisely divide that budget into specific audio segments and video frames, based on the complexity of the content and the redundancy in the time sequence. In essence, OmniDelta allows the model to “pay only for what it needs,” resulting in reduced memory usage and faster processing.

**The Trick**: Introducing the OmniDelta framework, which utilizes a “skill-driven” budget allocation strategy. A key innovation lies in two aspects: firstly, building an “skill pool” for audio and video, dynamically adjusting cross-modal budget allocation based on query intent to address the unreliability of direct similarity; and secondly, employing content awareness and local complexity strategies to redistribute budgets within each modality, prioritizing and discarding redundant frames to retain high-value segments. Experiments on the Qwen2.5-Omni-7B model showed a 22.0% reduction in GPU memory usage and a 1.64x improvement in end-to-end inference speed when only 25% of tokens were retained, redefining the efficiency-accuracy Pareto frontier under pruning.

**Startup Angle**:
Can enter the market for “multi-modal large model inference acceleration and GPU memory optimization middleware.” Targeting B-end scenarios such as video analysis and real-time voice interaction – which are highly sensitive to latency and have limited GPU memory (e.g., security monitoring, intelligent customer service) – it offers a dynamic budget allocation service based on intent recognition. By optimizing token allocation strategies, it helps clients improve multi-modal model inference speed by 64%, directly reducing the need to expand server capacity, and thus capturing the market for the practical implementation of large multi-modal models in vertical industries.

items.title: [Highly-rated paper] ReDesign: Recovering Editable Design Structures from Images via Agentic Decomposition
items.summary:
**Plain English**: Automatically convert ordinary images (such as design mockups) into editable vector files (in formats similar to Figma or Illustrator), addressing the pain points of designers who spend a lot of time and effort, have high manual costs, and struggle with version control when converting images.

items.title: 👑[ETH] Visual prompt engineering for video models
items.summary:
**Plain English**: Video large models now function similarly to text large models – their performance is largely determined by the “prompts” used. Traditionally, this involved text instructions. However, a recent paper has found that using AI to automatically transform “abstract sketches” from video footage into “high-resolution, realistic images” – a technique called “Visual Prompt Engineering” (VIPE) – allows video models to perform better on tasks requiring physical reasoning, and even surpasses the results achieved through simply scaling computational power (Test-time Scaling).

**The Trick**: The core concept is “Visual Prompt Engineering” (VIPE): This involves using image editing models to automatically transform abstract scenes from videos (such as sketches and diagrams) into high-fidelity, realistic visuals. Experiments have shown that this visual-level prompt optimization significantly improves the accuracy of video models in tasks requiring physical reasoning, and it’s more efficient than simply increasing computational resources, compared to traditional text prompts.

items.title: 👑[ETH / MIT] CodeNib: A Multi-View Data System for Serving Repository Context to Coding Agents
items.summary:
**Plain English**: Coding Agents are facing a challenge with “fragmentation” during development due to the separation of indexing, language servers, and historical records. This leads to redundant searches, loss of context, and difficulty in controlling costs. CodeNib has developed a “multi-view data system” that automatically generates three types of views – lexical, dense, and structural – for each code commit. This system precisely maps code outputs to their corresponding location within the codebase and provides unified service for search, symbol navigation, and context maintenance, effectively covering the entire “lifecycle” of the codebase.

**The Trick**: The core concept is “multi-view reuse + lifecycle mapping.” It no longer relies on a single index, instead dynamically generating three types of views – lexical, dense, and structural – for each code change, and establishing a strong mapping between code output and its relative position within the code repository. By maintaining continuity across edits, it integrates previously separate indexes, language servers, and history records into a single runtime. Experiments show that graph and vector updates improved by 8.7x and 25.4x, respectively, when the output matched an independent reconstruction. In static navigation scenarios, the real-time vs. static latency ratio achieved a 4.7x improvement, and through context strategies, reduced token consumption compared to traditional grep/read by 50%-87%.

**Startup Angle**:
Entering the “Code Agent Context Infrastructure” market. We are providing “code context service layers” for SaaS platforms, open-source communities, and large tech companies that possess extensive private codebases. This integrates previously disparate LSP (Language Server Protocol), Git history, and document indexing into a single runtime. By reducing redundant searches and token consumption, we directly lower the inference costs (token costs) and server load of AI code generation services, creating an “operating system-level middleware” for the age of code agents.

items.title: 👑[ETH / ICT] Temporal-Distance JEPA: Plan-Aware Representation Learning for Latent World Model Predictive Control
items.summary:
**Plain English**: The solution addresses the challenges of “offline data” and “online planning.” Traditional methods relied on Euclidean distance (straight-line distance) to predict future states, which led to inaccurate planning in complex tasks. The new approach extracts “temporal order” and “cross-trajectory comparison” from the original logs, directly embedding “time cost” into the model. This allows the model to not only understand “where” in the future, but also “which step is better,” transitioning from simply “visualizing” to “predicting and simulating along a timeline.”

**The Trick**: The core of this approach utilizes the TD-JEPA algorithm. Instead of relying solely on Euclidean distance for planning, it extracts “temporal distance” and “trajectory comparison” signals from offline logs. Specifically, it uses the temporal order of similar trajectories as positive samples and contrasts between different trajectories as negative samples, while also incorporating a “temporal consistency” constraint. This extracted “temporal cost” is then directly used in the planning stage. When the task relies on a topological structure, it replaces Euclidean distance as the planning cost. When it depends on contact geometry, it enhances Euclidean planning as a representation signal. Experiments show a success rate increase from 97.4% to 100% in dual-room tasks, and a 14.2 point improvement in the OGB-Cube task, effectively eliminating the performance gap between training and planning.

**Startup Angle**:
Can penetrate the “Embodied AI” market for offline data value discovery and planning optimization. Targeting scenarios like robotics and autonomous driving, which rely on large amounts of offline data but have weak online planning capabilities, it offers a “time-aware planning middleware” based on TD-JEPA. This helps companies significantly improve robot task success rates by leveraging the temporal structure within offline logs, without increasing online sensor costs, addressing the industry’s pain point of “having a lot of data but lacking accurate planning.”

items.title: 👑[CAS / COHERE / MIT] Human-in-the-Loop Signature Bootstrapping for UAV Hyperspectral PFM-1 Mine Detection
items.summary:

Traditionally, models were trained using ground-based terrain features or by training on the entire dataset – the latter being very slow. The new approach introduces a “human-in-the-loop” mechanism, where drones, using adaptive algorithms (like ACE), prioritize locking in high-confidence areas during flight, enabling rapid “human verification.” This achieves the same detection accuracy as training on the entire dataset, while requiring fewer flight cycles and reduced on-site verification.

items.title: 👑[ICT] VisualPatchWorld: Code World Models as Latent Structured Representations for Planning
items.summary:
**Plain English**: Transform “World Model” from a black box neural network or physics engine into directly executable code. This allows AI to simulate the physical world using code logic, enabling it to “predict” the future in a way that mimics a programmer, rather than relying solely on probabilistic predictions.

**The Trick**: VisualPatchWorld’s core is “qualitative dynamics + code fitting.” It first rapidly identifies fundamental physical rules (like gravity and collisions) using a small number of samples. Then, it automatically generates specific parameters using a code generator. The generated code model can be used like a simulator to predict, can be manually reviewed like a physics engine, and can be directly integrated into model prediction control (MPC) closed-loop systems.

items.title: [Highly-rated paper] Mapping CVEs to MITRE ATT&CK Techniques: A Curated Gold-Set Classifier and the Limits of LLM-Assisted Label Expansion
items.summary:

This paper demonstrates that a classifier trained on 1200 expert-level CVE data significantly doubled the recall rate compared to simply using vector similarity matching (Zero-shot). However, experiments decisively refuted the idea that “large models can automatically complete labels.” Using labels generated by LLMs to expand the training set actually *reduced* performance, leading to a decrease in coverage for rare attack techniques due to evaluation noise, resulting in a drop of 0.04 in the overall F1 score. The conclusion is clear: data quality – expert labeling – is the key, and “garbage data” generated by large models will only dilute the model’s potential.

**The Trick**: The core of this work involves building a multi-label classifier based on a “gold-standard dataset of expert data,” completely abandoning the inefficient chain of reasoning relying on CWE->CAPEC->ATT&CK.

1.  Data Cleaning and Evaluation Protocol Reconstruction: The research found significant fluctuation in evaluation results (Recall@5 varied by 0.05), due to noise in a small test dataset. By revising the protocol for selecting validation set checkpoints, evaluation errors were eliminated, demonstrating the stability of a purely expert data model (Recall@5 0.673).

2.  Validation of LLM Data Augmentation Failure: Through independent replication and scaled experiments (100-984 new CVEs), it was confirmed that the consistency between LLM-generated labels and expert annotations was only 0.39, providing no reliable benefit.

3.  Experiment-Driven Scaling Strategy: Experiments demonstrated that increasing the volume of expert manually annotated data consistently improves model performance, while increasing the volume of data generated by LLMs proved ineffective, and even introduced negative interference.

items.title: [Highly-Cited Paper] CAST: Game Solvers as Turn-Level Teachers for LLM Agents
items.summary:
**Plain English**: Addressing the challenge of “only knowing the outcome, not the process” – a problem with large models in long-term strategic games – this approach leverages game-solving algorithms’ state value changes. By making the implicit signal of “how to best proceed next” explicit, the model receives precise, immediate feedback at each step, significantly improving its ability to generalize and make decisions.

**The Trick**: The core of this approach utilizes the CAST framework, employing a “solver” as a teacher. It calculates the change in the solver’s state value function to derive advantage, which is then injected as a dense process reward signal into reinforcement learning. This method is based on the assumption of a soft optimal solver, enabling strategy distillation with just scalar values, and comprehensively outperforms baseline methods in complex tasks like Sokoban and Minesweeper. It also achieves state-of-the-art zero-sample performance in open-world environments like ALFWorld and WebShop.

items.title: [Highly-rated paper] DecoEvo: Score-Decoupled Co-Evolution of Solver and Rubric-Generator Skills in Text Space
items.summary:
**Plain English**: Large language models sometimes face a challenge when “self-evolving.” This happens because the evaluation criteria (Rubric) and problem-solving abilities (Solver) become intertwined. As a result, models may try to “please” the evaluation criteria by manipulating their responses, or the criteria may fail to cover new and complex problems, leading the models to get stuck in a loop.

DecoEvo addresses this by completely separating the “problem-solving” and “question generation” processes. This allows models to focus solely on specific metrics during problem-solving, while “question generators” can independently identify and address blind spots that the evaluation criteria haven’t yet covered. This allows for synchronized and independent evolution of both, ensuring the model becomes stronger in real-world scenarios.

**The Trick**: The core concept is the “decoupled collaborative evolution” mechanism. Traditional methods treat evaluation criteria (Rubric) as fixed benchmarks, leading to a situation where models can only “game” the existing standards during optimization. DecoEvo introduces a “decoupled” strategy: the Solver skill only receives feedback at the metric level, focusing on improving specific capabilities. The Rubric-Generator skill operates independently, using “demand coverage” and “response distinctiveness” to proactively identify implicit dimensions that the Solver hasn’t yet met. This mechanism breaks the causal chain between “gaming” and “evolution,” forcing the model to continuously iterate on genuine capabilities, rather than simply circling within the boundaries defined by the standards.

**Startup Angle**:
The startup can enter the market for “vertical industry large model continuous evolution middleware.” Specifically, they offer “dynamic evaluation standard generation + model capability decoupling optimization” for scenarios like financial risk control and legal compliance, where models require extreme robustness. This helps B-end clients address issues of “standard blind spots” in complex scenarios, leading to hallucinations or misinterpretations. They are transforming models from “static scoring tools” into “dynamic self-evolving engines,” directly improving their generalization ability and long-term value in real-world applications.

items.title: [Highly-rated paper] CoRT: Counterfactual Replay for Token-Level Rubric-Guided Policy Optimization
items.summary:
**Plain English**: The problem was that large models struggled when trained using “standardized scoring.” The reward signal was distributed evenly across the entire response, preventing the model from accurately identifying which specific words should be reinforced or penalized. CoRT addresses this with “counterfactual replay” – by comparing the same response in both “standard” and “non-standard” scenarios, it precisely calculates the weight for each token, enabling fine-grained reward allocation without needing a separate scoring model.

**The Trick**: The core concept is the “counterfactual replay” mechanism (CoRT). Instead of training an assisting scoring model, CoRT generates the same response under “with standard” and “without standard” prompts. By comparing the token counts’ likelihood in these two scenarios, it constructs token-level dependency weights. These weights are then used to redistribute the reward advantage of GRPO, ensuring the model can accurately learn the key features within the standard, while maintaining the simplicity and stability of the GRPO training framework.

**Startup Angle**:
Can enter the “vertical domain large model fine-tuning middleware” market. For companies in sectors like healthcare and law, which require strict standards for response format and logic, it offers a fine-grained reward allocation service based on CoRT, helping them significantly improve model adherence to specific standards while maintaining training stability, directly enhancing the compliance and professionalism of their B-end products.

items.title: 👑[ICT / MIT] OPERA: Offline Policy-guided Expert Routing and Adaptation for Universal Biomedical Image Analysis

During deployment, unlabeled test data is used to dynamically adjust class weights, combined with assessments of model consistency, enabling distribution adaptation without gradient updates, ensuring stable performance across devices and across different modalities.
